phases.title: Define Allocation Scopes For Foreground, Maintenance, Recovery, And Streaming
acceptance: foreground, maintenance, recovery, scrub, import/export, and streaming allocation envelopes are separately admitted and counted
unbounded buffers, copied payloads, rich diagnostics, materialized record sets, and background work memory cannot allocate outside admitted envelopes
fixed metadata exemptions are explicit, counted separately, constant-size, and independent of store scale and diagnostic richness
maintenance and scrub cannot steal foreground envelopes by convention
phases.instructions: Implement Allocation Admission Law and Fixed Metadata Allocation Rule inside this phase. Resident memory budgets do not catch all heap growth, so allocation scopes must be first-class proof-bearing resources. Foundational performance reports describe evidence only at export boundaries.
phases.qa_focus: Allocation envelopes by scope, fixed_metadata_allocation_exemption_suite, no ambient Rust heap success as admission, no rich diagnostics on hot paths without profile admission.

phases.title: Build Zero-Copy And Bounded-Copy Physical Record Views

bounded-copy views require admitted copy/materialization envelopes and exact copy counters
stale references, invalid header witnesses, expired leases, or profile-forbidden materialization deny before view construction
conflicting immutable/mutable views and dirty mutation or publication interactions deny or route through admitted counted bounded-copy/COW fallback

Dirtying or publishing a resident frame with incompatible live views must deny before mutation/publication or use an explicitly admitted bounded-copy/COW path with counters and dirty-state receipts.
phases.qa_focus: Zero-copy lifetime compile-fail proof, conflicting_view_and_dirty_mutation_suite, copy counter exactness, no semantic materialization to resolve physical view conflicts.

phases.qa_focus: speculative_work_memory_admission_suite, no hidden cache-hit inflation, lowered plans not executor redecision, no S.6 authority leakage.
